title: 8:00 AM. Every Day. (final build plan)
logline: An 18 s vertical Reel for AWSAVYA's daily-Instagram-ad service that reads as an ad from frame 0. The first frame already shows an "A SERVICE BY [AWSAVYA]" sticker, the offer "Your daily Instagram ad, made & posted." and a tilted phone with a fresh poster dropping in, which a split-flap stamp then marks "POSTED · 8:00 AM". A 1.5 s painted shot of Riya, busy and worried at her counter while her phone buzzes, carries the line "For your [bakery. / salon. / clinic. / coaching centre.]". Then the camera dives into the real AutoPostInsta app and follows one continuous move: you type one idea, AI writes the words, AI makes the poster (the hero moment: a beat of silence, yellow halftone dots print the photo, the poster assembles), you schedule it, and the status reads "Scheduled for 28 Nov, 8:00 am." A hard cut to signal yellow flips the date board SAT 28 NOV to TUE 01 DEC as example posters throw onto a stack, "Every day." slams in, and it closes on the pixel wordmark, "We'll build yours." and the poster's own yellow "TALK TO US · AWSAVYA.IN" button. The final frame loops cleanly back to frame 0.
look_spec:
DESIGN READ: "An ad for busy Indian shop owners scrolling with the sound off. The real AutoPostInsta screen does the work, one clear step per beat, with calm editorial confidence and no hype. Painted human context and printed-feeling product." Taste dials: visual_variance 6, motion_intensity 7, information_density 3.

PALETTE (max 4 on screen): paper #F5F4F8 (main field), ink #15131C (type, bezels, flap cells), graphite #57536A (secondary UI text only), signal yellow #FFC83D (the only accent). Yellow is always a filled shape (chip, slot block, button, halftone dots, the full-bleed S8 field) with ink text on it. Never yellow text or thin yellow strokes on paper (1.4:1). Never purple: on the host :root set --brand, --accent and --accent-2 all to #FFC83D, which removes the registry's #c5a3ff violet fallback. Leave day-6 (purple frosting) out everywhere. In the painted cutaway, PAL.ink and C.phone (#2B2233) become #15131C, and the indigo night sky becomes warm dawn #F2B575.

TYPE: Archivo 800 display, tracking -0.025em, left-aligned on an asymmetric grid (never a centred title on a gradient). Sizes: hook 112 px; S2 strip 110/84 px; S3 line 96 px; step lines 84 px; S8 slam 170 px; end line 140 px. Martian Mono for chips, flaps and the capsule, never under 42 px (capsule 46 px). The real UI is rebuilt vertical-native at 1.6x so its labels are 42 px or more on screen; the only exception is the poster's own small body line, which is image content. Fonts are local @font-face woff2 copied from D:/Projects/AutoPostInsta/video/autopost-ad-v2/assets/fonts (fallback: D:/Projects/AutoPostInsta/brand). Never Google imports, never Inter.

DEPTH AND MATERIAL: the S1 phone sits at perspective 1600 px, rotateY -14deg, rotateX 6deg. S3 uses a parallax dive with layer ratios 1.0/1.15/1.3. Phone, poster, stack cards and the S2 printed strip get real soft shadows (0 40px 80px rgba(21,19,28,.18); the strip gets 0 24px 48px rgba(21,19,28,.22) and a -1.5deg tilt, like a label stuck onto the watercolour). grain-overlay at 0.06 over everything, the painted plate included, so the two materials sit on one paper. Material changes on the beat: paper > painted watercolour (2.0) > paper app (3.5) > full-bleed yellow (13.0) > paper end card (15.0).

MOTION: everything sits on a 120 BPM grid (beat 0.5 s = 15 frames, bar 2.0 s). Cuts at 2.0 / 3.5 / 13.0 / 15.0; music dropout at 8.5; drop at 9.0. Shot lengths 2.0/1.5/1.5/2.0/1.5/2.5/2.0/2.0/3.0, so no length repeats three times in a row. Three transition meanings only: (1) hard cut, or velocity-matched cut-the-curve, means a new beat; (2) camera push/zoom (ui-focus-zoom, the parallax dive) means "look closer at this UI step"; (3) a same-rect match cut means "this becomes that" (preview card to hero poster, receded poster to the front stack card). Easings: expo.out / power4.out for kinetic type; back.out(1.6) for pops (0.8 > 1.05 > 1.0, settling in 3-5 frames); sine.inOut for every camera move; the components' sampled springs for the sheet and stack; power3.in for exits, about 40% shorter than entrances. 2-3 frames of anticipation before each tap. Never linear, never a fade-in. Text never moves while it is being read. Every paused frame must work as a still.

SAFE ZONE: all text and logos inside x 65-1015, y 270-1248. Nothing important in the bottom 35%: phone bodies and poster imagery may run below, text may not. One focal text element per frame. On-screen text stays under 5 words/s.

BANNED BY NAME: centred title on a gradient; fade-in-everything; grids of squares; corner HUD text or frames; a logo only at the end; the same transition on every cut; any webgpu / webgpu-shader / WebGL shader-transition / liquid-glass / vfx-* block; motion-blur; backdrop-filter; native-notification-pop (AutoPostInsta is a web app with no push notifications); Instagram's logo, icons or chrome; feed handles like '@your.shop'; invented shop names; count-up, star-rating-fill, testimonial-card, logo-wall, trust-strip; hearts or likes; hype words; emoji.

THEME TOKENS (index.html :root): --bg:#F5F4F8; --fg:#15131C; --muted:#57536A; --surface:#FFFFFF; --border:rgba(21,19,28,.12); --brand:#FFC83D; --accent:#FFC83D; --accent-2:#FFC83D; --font-display:'Archivo'; --font-body:'Archivo'; --font-mono:'Martian Mono'; --ease-entrance:cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1); --ease-exit:cubic-bezier(.32,0,.67,0); --ease-primary:cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1).

PROJECT: run node "C:/Users/vivek/.claude/skills/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" init D:/Projects/AutoPostInsta/video/autopost-ad-v3 --skip-skills --skill=hyperframes. Root 1080x1920, 30 fps, data-duration 18 (540 frames). Install each preset from inside autopost-ad-v3 with: node "C:/Users/vivek/.claude/skills/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs" add <name> --json. Keep the id prefixes and mount with data-composition-src. Sub-compositions: hook (0-2), painted (2-3.5), dive (3.5-5), app-take (5-13: ONE ui-focus-zoom camera rig over a single tall vertical-native column of the real cards, plus a hero-poster layer and a publish-sheet layer), everyday (13-15), endcard (15-18). The root also holds a grain host and three <audio> tags with ids (music, sfx, vo).

ASSETS: (a) copy fonts, awsavya-logo.png, poster-photo.jpg and poster-bakery.jpg from autopost-ad-v2/assets. (b) make_poster.py reads its source photos from the session scratchpad, which can be wiped, so first copy bake-1..5.png and reel/1-problem.jpg into autopost-ad-v3/assets/src and repoint SRC. Change .resize((270, 338)) to (720, 900) and export only the hero, day-2 (loaves), day-3 (cake) and day-5 (cinnamon rolls). Never day-6. (c) The hero poster in S1 and S6 is LIVE HTML over poster-photo.jpg: the 'FOR BAKERIES' label, the headline 'Fresh bakes. Posted before you open.', the offer line, the pixel wordmark, and the 'TALK TO US · AWSAVYA.IN' button, laid out exactly like make_poster.py (W 1080, H 1350, photo band 350-1060). All brand, URL and CTA text is real text. (d) Painted plate assets/riya-cut.mp4: see S2.

Left-aligned headline at x 65, y 380-740. Lower right: a phone (device-frame-stage, 500 px wide, x 500-1000, top y 790, rotateY -14 / rotateX 6, ink bezel, long soft shadow), already 70% risen at f0. On its screen the live hero poster is mid-drop from the top of the screen at f0 and lands by 0.45 s. No feed handle, no notification, no Instagram chrome. At 1.0 s a split-flap stamp (ink cells, paper Martian Mono 42 px) springs onto the poster's top-left corner (x ~440-860, y ~805-865) and flips '7:59' to read 'POSTED · 8:00 AM'. 'Posted' is the app's own status word. The sticker exits upward at 1.25 s, which caps brand time.
shots.onscreen_text: Sticker: 'A SERVICE BY' + [AWSAVYA pixel wordmark] (0.00-1.25). Headline: 'Your daily / Instagram ad, / made & posted.' with ink text on a yellow block behind 'made & posted.'. Flap stamp: 'POSTED · 8:00 AM' (from 1.0). Poster (image content): 'FOR BAKERIES' / 'Fresh bakes. Posted before you open.' / 'TALK TO US · AWSAVYA.IN'.
shots.motion: Headline per-word-rise from f0 (first word 40% risen at f0, 3-frame stagger, expo.out), fully set by 0.40 s. It holds still to 1.75 s, giving about 1.4 s to read. marker-highlight in highlight mode wipes the yellow block in behind 'made & posted.' at 0.50 on the beat (expo.out, 0.25 s). The phone settles with one overshoot by 0.6 s. The poster lands with back.out(1.6) (0.8 > 1.05 > 1.0). Sticker: spring-pop, at scale 0.85 on f0 and 1.0 by f6; exits at 1.25 (power3.in, 0.2 s). Flap stamp: spring-pop in at 0.90, flaps 0.09 s each, landing on the 1.0 beat. Whole-frame camera push 1.00 > 1.04 (sine.inOut, 2 s). camera-shake 'handheld' at about 30% amplitude, on the phone layer only.

They swap at peak speed to the painted plate, which enters from below and decelerates (power4.out, about 0.25 s). The whoosh starts 20 ms before the move.
shots.presets: device-frame-stage, per-word-rise, marker-highlight, spring-pop, split-flap-board (cell and drum code lifted into a small 1-row stamp component, font set to Martian Mono), camera-shake, cut-the-curve, grain-overlay (global)

Riya kneads dough at the counter, centre frame, with the oven glow behind her and a warm dawn window (no indigo). The phone on the counter buzzes at 2.5 s with painted vibration marks; she glances at it, worried (sweat drops), and goes back to the dough. She is a busy owner, not a client: she never uses the app on screen. Over the window and clock area (x 65-1015, y 285-545), a crisp printed paper strip, tilted -1.5deg with a real shadow, carries the trade roll. The old burned-in 'NO TIME TO POST?' plate text is removed.
shots.onscreen_text: 'For your' (Archivo 800, 110 px, ink) over a masked slot on a filled yellow block, with ink words at 84 px: 'bakery.' > 'salon.' > 'clinic.' > 'coaching centre.' The slot is sized to the widest word, so nothing reflows.
shots.motion: The plate and strip ride in on cut-the-curve's incoming half. The painted camera is already drifting in the plate. kinetic-type-swap is edited so the sentence is fully visible within 0.15 s of mount (IN_BASE cut from 2.25 s). 'bakery.' shows from 2.05, then swaps at 2.40, 2.75 and 3.05 (mount-relative cues 0.40, 0.75, 1.05), each a masked upward roll on expo.out over 0.28 s. 'coaching centre.' holds 0.45 s. A 2% punch-in on each swap decays over 5 frames. Painted flour puffs land on the 2.0 and 3.0 beats.
shots.transition_out: Hard cut to paper on the 3.5 beat (a new beat, new material). A soft kick lands on the cut.

voiceover.text: Run a bakery, a salon, a clinic?
Type an idea, or pick one.
We'll build yours. AWSAVYA dot in.

captions_style: No burned-in word-by-word or karaoke captions. The kinetic lines are the captions, written for a muted viewer. Every voiceover idea has an on-screen counterpart within about 1 s: the S2 trade roll (L1), Riya's worried face and buzzing phone (L2), 'We built it for ourselves first.' (L3), the YOU/AI step lines (L4-L7), the 'Every day.' slam (L8), and the end card (L9). Each reinforces the voice without repeating it word for word. That follows the reviewer rule never to put the same words in two places in one window, and it keeps one focal text per frame. Step-line style: a Martian Mono 42 px chip ('YOU' or 'AI', ink on yellow) followed by an Archivo 800 84 px ink line, on a paper header bar at y 270-390, entering with a masked line-swap rise (expo.out, 0.3 s) and swapping on step changes. All text sits inside x 65-1015 and y 270-1248, never under 42 px, never yellow on paper. Accessibility: export an .srt of the voiceover from the word timestamps (brand spelled AWSAVYA) and attach it as viewer-toggleable closed captions where Meta allows, or turn on Instagram's auto-captions. Do not burn it in.
sound_plan:
FOUR LAYERS: voice, music, SFX, and a faint room tone under the painted beat. Everything except the voice is synthesized in numpy: adapt D:/Projects/AutoPostInsta/video/painted-ad/make_audio.py into autopost-ad-v3/make_audio.py, driven by an event list taken from the shot table.

risks_and_mitigations:
1) A THIRD 'STILL LOOKS THE SAME'. The base is paper plus app UI, which the owner rejected twice. Mitigations: a painted watercolour beat at 2.0; a full-bleed yellow beat at 13.0; a 3D-tilted phone and parallax dive; real shadows; grain; printed-strip labels; and a different primary subject, composition and motion register in every beat (phone result / painted person / phone dive / typing / streaming fields / hero poster / publish sheet / yellow stack and flap / wordmark). Before rendering, run the distinctness gate on a contact sheet: no two beats share a primary subject, the poster signature appears in only 2 beats (S1 small, S6 hero), and the answer to 'could this be any other studio's ad?' is no, because of the 8:00 AM flap built from the app's own status string.

2) STORY CONTRADICTION (a shop's feed posting AWSAVYA's ad). Fixed: no feed handle and no '@your.shop'. The demo shows AWSAVYA making its OWN ad for bakery owners (typed idea 'An ad for bakery owners', which yields its 'We build you an app...' copy and the 'TALK TO US · AWSAVYA.IN' button), framed by the true line 'We built it for ourselves first'. The stack is labelled 'EXAMPLE WEEK'. Riya is shown only as a busy owner and never uses the app or appears as a client.

3) INVENTED FEATURES. The iOS push banner is dropped (AutoPostInsta is a web app). There is no 'button field' and no 'Writing…' label. Only exact strings checked against web/public/index.html and app.js are used: 01 Idea, What should this post be about?, Give me an idea, Write it with AI, 02 Words, Who it's for, Headline, Offer line, 03 Image, Make image with AI, 04 Preview, 05 Publish, Schedule, Post now, Add to queue, Buffer draft, Date and time, Add Instagram's "AI info" label, Publish, 'Scheduled for 28 Nov, 8:00 am.' The stamp uses the app's own status word 'Posted'.

4) PURPLE LEAKS. day-6 (purple frosting) is excluded. The painted kit's PAL.ink and C.phone (#2B2233) and the indigo sky (#2E3570 / #3B3D7A) are patched in the riyacut.js copy only, because PAL is shared with clawd.js. --accent-2 is set to yellow. Every preset's 'accent' enum is ignored in favour of the tokens.

5) PRESET EDITS, each a small source change. kinetic-type-swap: IN_BASE 2.25 s cut to about 0.15 s, cues 0.40/0.75/1.05. spring-stack-shuffle: CUE_MIN 0.85 to 0.1, mounted at 13.0. split-flap-board is a 1920x1080 block: lift its cell and drum code into two small components (S1 stamp, S8 date strip) and switch ui-monospace to Martian Mono. wordmark-tiles: crop tiles from the PNG, 10 columns, 25 ms stagger, about 0.8 s. parallax-device-dive / device-frame-stage: replace the placeholder UI, match the bezels. ui-focus-zoom: set the duration to 8.0 and keep the move clamps in mind when placing cues. hw-callout-circle: no label, so its handwritten font never appears. grain-overlay: change the infinite hf-grain-noise loop to 36 iterations or check fails. Override the Inter / system font fallbacks via the tokens.

6) PAINTED PLATE. Stale frames: render.mjs --frames is resumable, so move painted-ad/out/frames aside or use --clip. Quality: the double encode softens watercolour, so encode at CRF 12. Time: 45 frames at about 3.5 s each is a few minutes. Fallback if the plate looks wrong or will not render: swap S2 for a full-bleed ink beat with the same paper-on-yellow trade roll. Timing is unchanged, but the people signal is lost.

7) RENDER COST ON IRIS XE. Every preset is CPU/GSAP; there is no WebGPU, WebGL, html-in-canvas, backdrop-filter or motion-blur. halftone-dissolve is mounted only at the 680x447 photo window, with 18 columns or fewer. The cut-the-curve seam blur is capped at 8 px for about 3 frames. The S8 dim uses a scrim, not a blur. Draft-render S1 and S6 first; use bounded timelines only (no repeat:-1).

8) VOICE. The US accent may feel less native (an optional variant with Hinglish kinetic lines costs one render). The name splice is the weakest point: check level, pitch and room tone at 16.25 by ear. If 'or pick one' makes the take run long, cut it before pushing speed past 1.05. 'AI' must be read as 'A.I.'

9) TEXT DENSITY AND THE SAFE ZONE. The step line always enters first and exits before the poster's own headline (9.55). The camera makes only one UI region readable at a time. Snapshot-check 'coaching centre.' at 84 px inside the strip, and the Publish button and status above y 1248. The hook headline gets about 1.4 s still: if testing shows it is too short, extend S1 by one beat rather than shrink the text.

10) BRAND SCREEN TIME. Sticker 0-1.25 plus end card 15-18 is about 24% of the runtime, under Meta's 25% guidance. The poster's own button is product content. Do not lengthen either.

11) CLAIM WORDING. 'made & posted' and 'every single day' describe the service as briefed (AI writes the copy and makes the poster; it posts on schedule). The demo visibly shows the person typing the idea, so nothing implies zero input. No numbers, prices, clients, ratings, results or testimonials appear anywhere, and no count-up / rating / testimonial / logo-wall presets are used.

12) POSTER PROVENANCE. The week posters are drawn by make_poster.py, which copies the app's canvas. They are labelled EXAMPLE. Better: regenerate those 4 through the real app before the final render. make_poster.py's SRC points at the wipeable session scratchpad, so copy the source photos into the project first.

13) CALENDAR. 28 Nov 2026 is a Saturday and 1 Dec is a Tuesday (today is Fri 27 Nov 2026), so the flap sequence is correct.

QA LOOP: npx hyperframes check --json, fixing every error. Then snapshot --review at every 0.5 s (36 frames), checking that frame 0 has motion, brand, product and offer; every pause works as a still; there is one focal text per frame; all text is inside y 270-1248. Then a 0.25x motion review for spring and ease quality, then npx hyperframes beats, then a draft render. Final: H.264 High 4.2, 10 Mbps, yuv420p, +faststart. A/B: hook variants B 'Bakery owners: your daily Instagram ad, done.' and C 'We built this for our own Instagram.' change only S1's headline variable, so each costs one extra render.
why_this_beats_previous_versions:
1) IT IS AN AD BY FRAME 0, which is where the painted cartoon failed ('other than the last 2-3 seconds it's just a video'). Frame 0 already shows the service label ('A SERVICE BY' + wordmark), the offer as kinetic type ('Your daily Instagram ad, made & posted.', set by 0.4 s), the product (the real poster landing in a phone) and motion. Sound carries a second hook: the voice calls out the viewer's trade at 0.25 s. Brand and message land inside Meta's first-3-to-5-seconds window.

2) IT IS NOT FLAT, which is where v1 and v2 failed ('looks flat, still the same'). It changes material on the beat: paper > painted watercolour > paper app > full-bleed yellow > paper. It adds real depth (3D phone, parallax dive, long shadows, printed strips, grain) and physics (springs with overshoot, a stack with mass, a camera that pushes toward every tap). Every beat has a different primary subject, so it never plays as re-captioned white cards.

3) THE PRODUCT DOES THE SELLING. The real AutoPostInsta screen is on screen from 3.6 s to 13 s in one continuous camera move, using only its exact strings. The product appears three times in different forms (posted result, live build, example week), and the proof is the true scheduled status, not invented numbers.

4) THE BOLDNESS GOES INTO ONE MOMENT, the poster printing itself after a beat of silence, and that moment is the product. The concept is built from a real string in the app ('Scheduled for 28 Nov, 8:00 am.'), which gives a split-flap 8:00 AM device no other studio's ad could use.

5) IT IS TRUE AND COHERENT. It shows AWSAVYA making its own ad with the tool it built for itself ('We built it for ourselves first'), labels the example week, and uses no shop handle, push banner, client, number or testimonial. The end line 'We'll build yours.' makes clear this is a studio service.

6) IT KEEPS WHAT THE OWNER LIKED: 1.5 s of the painted Riya world brings back warmth and a person doing everyday work, rendered in minutes without the fragile phone-tracking pipeline. The voice is one natural Sarah take with the owner-approved brand-name clip spliced in, instead of line-by-line TTS.

7) IT FOLLOWS THE PLATFORM RESEARCH without stacking multipliers. Speech plus music; the CTA shown and spoken at the same moment; brand in two positions for about 24% of the runtime; features backing the message; text inside the Reels safe zone and readable muted; an 18 s length; a clean loop.

8) IT CAN BE BUILT ON THIS PC: 24 CPU-only registry presets, each with one job, no WebGPU or WebGL, render-heavy effects confined to small regions, and hook variants that cost one render each.
